_README: Executable half of .claude/DATA_QUALITY_TRACKER.md. The markdown holds the
narrative; this holds the one thing prose cannot do — answer 'is it still
broken?' by being RUN.
WHY: on 2026-08-12 the tracker said DQ-54 was 'Open — report-only' when it
had been fixed and merged that morning, and its own row said 'three call
sites' when there were nine. Its header said Last Updated 2026-08-08. A
hand-written status decays silently, and this repo has the receipts: #398
hid for ten weeks, DQ-54's prose recurred in four days.
THE RATCHET RUNS BOTH WAYS — that is the whole point:
declared 'fixed' + check FAILS  -> red. A regression, or a fix that never was.
declared 'open'  + check PASSES -> red. Silently fixed; the ledger is lying
the other way and nobody would ever look.
Only the second direction catches the failure mode that actually hurt here.
COVERAGE: every DQ id in the markdown must appear here. A new row without an
entry fails the coverage test, so the ledger cannot grow un-checkable rows.
Same shape as scripts/check_test_quarantine.py, which already works this way.
check: null is HONEST, not a TODO to hide behind. It means nobody has written
a falsifiable check yet, and the count of nulls is reported on every run so
the gap stays visible. An invented check that cannot fail is what produced
DQ-30's '0% drift' verification — worse than no check.

What changed is that they can now be counted. The floor stays in the query rather than being raised to today's number, because raising a floor to match a measurement is how a ratchet stops meaning anything - the row is simply open until it comes down. Root cause traced in scripts/dcp_extract_changed.py: _maybe_toc_override() opens the PDF and builds a list of every page's cleaned text, then (when that doesn't override) _extract_sequential() opens the SAME PDF again and does a second full page-by-page pass -- each pass accumulates pdfplumber's per-page objects (char/line/table/image data) for the whole document's lifetime, which is fine for a normal few-MB chapter but not for a 139MB one. Corroborating evidence from this session's OWN work (not just the production log): canterbury_bankstown/chapter-6-2-bankstown-city-centre is the SAME council's second-largest chapter (117,829,367 bytes) and has not yet been re-extracted since, so it carries the identical unconfirmed risk; ku_ring_gai/section-b-part-14e-lindfield-local-centre (35,405,674 bytes) was one of three ku_ring_gai chapters that reproducibly could not complete the (much lighter-weight) dcp_fidelity_gate.py grading pass within 300s across two independent attempts, while ashfield/chapter-d-precinct-guidelines (20,607,908 bytes) graded a full 638-row chapter without issue in the same session -- consistent with large file size being a real but imprecise proxy (page count, two-column layout, and embedded raster map/diagram images likely matter as much as raw bytes, per the [preflight] TWO-COLUMN warnings visible in the same production log for every large chapter listed). PROPOSED FIX DIRECTION (not built, not started): detect an oversized PDF ahead of extraction and split it into smaller physical PDFs (pypdf/pikepdf page-range slicing, cheap IO-level copy, no content parsing) before running the existing per-chapter extraction pipeline on each chunk, bounding peak memory to one chunk's page count instead of the whole document. Chosen over the alternative of upgrading Railway's container memory because a memory-ceiling fix does not scale with future, larger PDFs (this project's own DCPs keep growing via amendment) while a chunking fix does. The one real design risk, called out before any code is written: a clause can legitimately straddle a chunk boundary (this whole session's separate DQ-97 work fixed several defects caused by exactly this shape of problem, one level down in the pipeline) -- a correct implementation needs overlapping chunk boundaries and de-duplication when stitching per-chunk results back together, not a naive even split. User explicitly chose 'register now, build later' over pausing other in-progress work to design this immediately.
DQ-98.update_2026-09-10: THE FIX SHIPPED, AND IT IS NOT THE ONE THIS ROW DESCRIBED. This row proposed splitting oversized PDFs into overlapping chunks, and named a 139MB canterbury_bankstown chapter as the cause. Measured, that diagnosis was wrong twice over. (1) It named _maybe_toc_override and _extract_sequential as the two full passes; _maybe_toc_override only runs for woollahra and leichhardt, so for canterbury_bankstown the second pass is actually _maybe_route_via_ocr. (2) It framed the problem as oversized PDFs. It was not. pdfplumber caches every page's parsed objects for the life of the PDF object and nothing dropped them, so memory climbed across the WHOLE batch: a 4.3MB ashfield chapter peaked at 611 MB and left 214 MB resident. Three chapters in one process peaked at 1,361 MB and held 628 MB afterwards. WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD (PR #1073): each page is released after it is read (flush_cache plus the textmap lru_cache -- both needed, measured separately at 626 MB and 1,325 MB against 1,356 MB with neither, and 426 MB with both), and the PDF work now runs in its own process so a SIGKILL cannot take the batch down. Output proven byte-identical to the previous code on three real chapters covering both extraction paths, same sha256 over sections and over tables. THE 30MB GUARD IS GONE, deliberately: after the page fix, peak memory does not track file size at all -- ku_ring_gai/section-b-part-14e is 35MB and peaks at 726 MB while canterbury_bankstown/chapter-7-6 is 139MB and peaks at 440 MB. A size threshold blocked seven chapters that extract fine and would have waved the heaviest one through. Do not reintroduce one. Five of the seven were extracted locally to confirm; the two city_of_sydney chapters have no R2 URL and could not be tested, which is the untested-file case process isolation exists to survive. THE PROBE ALSO CHANGED, and that is half the point. It counted chapters over 30MB, so it could never reach 0 while large councils exist -- a check watching a field its own fix had abandoned. It now counts large chapters that have NEVER been extracted: 3 today, and 0 once the nightly run clears them. Left declared OPEN rather than fixed until a production run proves it, because everything above was measured on a developer machine.

DQ-103.passes_when: exit 0 - no served row is left reading ALL on a key its config entry declined to decide while its own text carries evidence for a narrower answer. DQ-103.red_when: `tag_with_provenance` discards a row's own text evidence because SOME OTHER key of the same config entry was decided.
DQ-103.note: Found 2026-09-23. `tag_with_provenance` guards text extraction with `if text and not config` - so a matched entry suppresses the regex for BOTH keys, including one the entry deliberately omitted. `config_silent` means 'an entry matched and nobody decided this key' (ApplicabilityTagger._resolve), so suppressing evidence on its account is a non-decision overruling data that exists. The row ends up ALL, so nothing is hidden from anyone; it is served to properties its own text does not reach, on no authority, which is the same unauditable ALL that DQ-33 was opened for. Not described as 'safe': an inapplicable control shown to a property is still a wrong answer, and calling the direction safe is how a row like this gets deprioritised forever. WIDENED THE SAME DAY, before it had ever run green: the first version counted DEV TYPES only, and the suppression is per-ENTRY not per-key, so an entry that names dev types and omits zones discards the row's zone evidence identically and was not counted - the check could have read zero with the defect fully present on the other column, which is exactly `feedback-a-check-can-watch-the-field-the-fix-abandoned`. Counting both keys took the measurement 500 -> 744 across 22 -> 27 documents, concentrated in waverley (257), campbelltown part 3 (111) and the city_of_sydney sections. Caught by the Sol cross-review at the push gate. The probe runs the TAGGER over the served corpus rather than reading the stored column, deliberately: the defect is in the tagger, not in any one stored row. NOT fixed in the same change as the Campbelltown and Canterbury-Bankstown configs: the guard is shared by all six config-driven councils, so lifting it re-tags waverley, woollahra, city_of_sydney and ku_ring_gai at the same time and every resulting narrowing needs adjudicating against its own chapter first.

There is no judgement to make about that, and the question should never have been put to a person. A PDF laid out right-to-left in places, usually inside a figure or a table, returns whole words mirrored. NOTHING DETECTED IT: _AUTO_REJECT_REASONS held garbled_glyphs, junk_ref and emptied_by_strip, none of which names this, so the row became `pending` rather than being rejected for a re-read -- against the pipeline's own rule that a row which cannot be proven is rejected and the chapter retries, and only genuine ambiguity reaches a person. Now detected at enqueue AND counted here, because the enqueue gate cannot reach what is already live. Reads 27 served rows across city_of_sydney, canterbury_bankstown and ku_ring_gai. THE DETECTOR IS EVIDENCE-BASED, not a substring probe: the obvious version, looking for 'kcabtes'/'nimm'/'xamm' as substrings, matched 40 served rows of which 35 were false positives because those letter runs occur inside ordinary words -- shipping that as an auto-REJECT would have thrown real controls away. A token counts only when its own reversal is a word this domain uses and the token itself is not, and only when two distinct such tokens appear in one provision. The vocabulary is imported from dcp_extract_changed so the probe and the gate cannot drift apart. DISTINCT FROM DQ-78, which counts runs of single letters: neither sees the other, and on 2026-09-23 DQ-78 read 34 while this read 27.

DQ-105.passes_when: exit 0 - no council serves rules that fall through to every development type for want of a config. Reachable ONLY by writing the configs from each council's own Application sections; deleting a council's rows would also take this to zero and is not the fix. A council with no config but ZERO rows falling through is printed as WATCHED and not counted - computed from the rows, never a named allowlist, so it is counted again the moment one row falls through.
DQ-105.red_when: a council serves rules with no config behind them AND at least one of them falls through, so its rules apply to every development type by fallthrough rather than by decision - and DQ-33's global floor is too coarse to notice, having had 234 rows of headroom on 2026-09-23.
DQ-105.note: Opened 2026-09-23 while answering 'does today's work cover future LGAs?'. The answer is mostly yes and the exception is this row. Everything that judges TEXT is universal: `classify_row_fidelity` takes no council argument, so reversed text (DQ-104), garbled glyphs, junk refs and emptied provisions are caught for any council from its first extraction, and the fidelity gate grades every row against its own source page regardless of who published it. The applicability config is the one onboarding step nothing can derive - a hand-written file recording which zones and development types each chapter binds, read from that chapter's own Application section. WHY DQ-33 DOES NOT COVER IT: DQ-33 is a single global count against a floor of 1,158 that may only fall. Measured 2026-09-23 it read 924, i.e. 234 rows of HEADROOM - so a newly onboarded council could publish 234 rules applying to every development type and nothing would go red. A total hides a per-council regression (feedback-counting-is-not-comparing), and what it hides here is precisely the non-automatic step. COUNTS COUNCILS, NOT ROWS, deliberately: the defect is that a council has no config, while how many of its rows currently fall through depends on whether the text regex happened to find a zone or a type in each one, which is noise that moves on every re-extraction. Reads 7 of 14 serving councils: parramatta (616 served, 341 falling through), blacktown (125/56), northern_beaches (99/63), penrith (81/55), hornsby (58/24), georges_river (33/19), cumberland (29/0). THE PROBE GOT ITS OWN QUESTION WRONG TWICE, both times by asking something ADJACENT to what the tagger asks, and both are pinned as tests. (1) It first compared each `source_council` string to COUNCIL_CONFIGS. The tagger keys on DOCUMENT_ID, so `inner_west` was reported as unconfigured on the strength of 11 rows - 10 from 'Marrickville_DCP_2011__...' and 1 from 'Ashfield_DCP_2007__...' - which the tagger resolves perfectly well, 10 of the 11 already tagged. Inner West is the most deeply configured council in the product; those rows simply carry the parent slug in source_council while naming a predecessor plan in their document_id, and only the latter is consulted. (2) It then resolved each document_id with an EMPTY provision text. Waverley and Woollahra key on a section code that _extract_section_code reads OUT OF THE TEXT, so both resolved to nothing and waverley was reported as unconfigured while serving 392 rows with ZERO fallthrough - which was itself the proof its config works. Now resolved per ROW with that row's own text. A council is unconfigured only when NOT ONE of its served rows reaches a config; a council where some chapters resolve and others do not is DQ-102's population.

DQ-107.passes_when: exit 0 - no section code carries two scope statements naming development types that cannot both be true. ⚠ THE OBVIOUS FIX DOES NOT WORK: adding one dcp_chapter_registry row per sub-part, all pointing at the same PDF, would make EACH of them extract the WHOLE document. DQ-108.note: Opened 2026-09-24 while verifying the formulate stage before running it on 13,909 provisions. DQ-114.red_when: a served rule is shown to every development type, or in every zone, on a source the schema itself calls undetermined - an entry matched and left the key undecided (config_silent), the text named zones this council does not have so the tagger fell back to ALL (filtered_to_all), there was nothing to match against (no_document_id), or the row was never tagged (NULL) - never because anyone decided it applies broadly.
DQ-114.note: THE ROW DQ-33 ASKED FOR, widened. DQ-33's note ends 'SEPARATE AND LARGER: ... that gap is not counted here and needs its own row.' Measured 2026-09-27: 4,374 key-decisions (dev types 2,859 silent + 36 untagged; zones 1,400 silent + 43 filtered_to_all + 36 untagged) against 17,440 served rows in 237 documents. COUNTED PER KEY on purpose: tag_with_provenance suppresses per-ENTRY, so an entry that names dev types and omits zones is silent on zones alone, and a per-row count would let a column go fully undecided without moving - feedback-a-check-can-watch-the-field-the-fix-abandoned. NOT DQ-103: that is the subset whose own text carries discarded evidence, fixable in code by stopping the discard (1,021 of these); the remainder needs a person to read the chapter. The largest single population is Wollongong chapter_b1_residential, 584 served rows 100% silent - and its config is CORRECT to be silent at chapter level, because the chapter as a whole names no development type while its sections 4, 5 and 6 each cover one. So part of reaching zero is a section-level key the config format does not have yet; every one of the 4,331 rows carries a ref_number that encodes its section, so the unit exists in the data already. city_of_sydney declares 0 scope keys across 7 entries and is entirely in this count.

DQ-115.note: Registered 2026-09-27 as the half that makes DQ-114 enforceable. DQ-114 on its own is clearable by typing ['ALL'] across all 193 declared keys: both counts would fall and every served answer would be worse, which is exactly 'the config file was written, so it was called done' - the failure this whole effort exists to remove. The configs are not sloppy; they are good and their evidence is real. Wollongong's entries quote chapter scope sections verbatim and B1 omits dev types with a stated reason. The defect is the MEDIUM: a Python comment is exactly as trustworthy as whoever typed it and is invisible to every consumer. Measured 193 of 193 declared keys with no machine-readable evidence, across 13 distinct configs - canterbury-bankstown 85, woollahra 50, warringah 14, parramatta 12, wollongong 9, waverley 6, ku_ring_gai 5. Aliases are de-duplicated by IDENTITY, not by name (ku_ring_gai/ku-ring-gai, city_of_sydney/sydney_dcp, canterbury_bankstown/canterbury-bankstown point at the same dict), or one missing sentence would count twice and the number would move when an alias was added. The probe also walks a `sections` bucket no config uses yet, so section-level entries are covered from the first one written rather than after someone remembers. It is the first probe in that file that needs no database, so needs_db is now carried per probe: opening a connection for a question the database is never asked would report exit 2 (UNKNOWN) instead of an answer.

DQ-116.passes_when: exit 0 - no served rule's own text says that rule has been repealed. ⚠ The earlier wording said this was 'reachable ONLY by re-reading the chapter' and that a by-hand fix was wrong. That was written before the source was read and it is withdrawn: the council's CURRENT chapter itself prints 'B3.3 Floorplate (Repealed)', so a re-read reproduces the row exactly. The row was FAITHFUL; the defect was carrying a repealed section in the served set as an actionable control. Reachable by marking such a row not-actionable, which is what it is. NOT reachable by deleting the row or editing its words - it is the council's own text and the evidence for its own exclusion.
DQ-116.red_when: a control the council has repealed is served as live, with a page number and a verbatim quote behind it - which is the most convincing way to be wrong, because every signal a reader uses to check us agrees.
DQ-116.note: Registered 2026-09-27 as the SECTION-level sibling of the document-level hard reject in dcp_extract_changed.detect_repealed_stamp, which already exists and works. The document guard cannot see this shape because nothing is wrong with the document: the chapter is in force, and a section inside it was repealed and marked in place. COUNTED BY POSITION, NOT VOCABULARY, and that distinction is the whole row: 68 served rows carry repeal wording and 67 of them are CORRECT to serve. `(a) (Repealed) (b) not have an area more than 25 m2` is NSW drafting convention - the repealed paragraph is left in place, marked, so the lettering of the surviving paragraphs does not shift - and flagging it would push toward deleting text the council deliberately kept. So the test is where the mark SITS: the section's own title carrying it, or the council writing the sentence outright. The document-level rule learned the same lesson from a false positive on a heritage chapter's sentence about a lighthouse ('This was later replaced by a number of lighthouses'), which passive-voice grammar cannot separate from a repeal stamp. The probe imports detect_repealed_section from dcp_extract_changed rather than restating the pattern, so there is one definition, not two. Reads 2 on 2026-09-27. woollahra B3.3 Floorplate is unambiguous. nsw_statewide 3.29 is a SEPP sunset clause and is DELIBERATELY left for a person: whether 'This section is repealed at the end of 30 June 2023' governs the section it sits in, or was bundled in from a neighbouring provision by the extractor, cannot be decided without reading the instrument, and interpreting a regulation is exactly what this repo refuses to automate. The probe returns the matched sentence as evidence rather than a bare flag, so the adjudication starts from the council's own words. ⚠ CORRECTED 2026-09-27, same day, after reading the source PDF: for the woollahra row the harm runs the OTHER WAY and it is worse than 'a dead control is served'. The council's CURRENT chapter — source-pdfs/dcps/woollahra/v1.4-2026-09-15/chapter-b3-general-development.pdf, 105 pages — has B3.3 Floorplate ALIVE on page 21 with a real control (the floorplate applies to development other than dwelling houses, semi-detached dwellings, secondary dwellings and dual occupancies in R2; maximum total floorplate is the buildable area times 1.65). The word 'repeal' appears ZERO times in all 105 pages. Two rows exist for B3.3: id 121802 carries that live text, was last modified 2026-09-15 (the PDF's own version date) and is is_current=FALSE; id 127014 carries '(Repealed)', was last modified 2026-09-18, version_count 1, and is is_current=TRUE. So a run on 18 September wrote text that is NOT IN THE SOURCE DOCUMENT and superseded a live binding control with it. We are not serving a dead rule; we are HIDING A LIVE ONE, and no served woollahra row carries the 1.65 factor. The registry makes this invisible: provisions_extracted_from_hash EQUALS content_hash (114475891aa8740d), so the row asserts it came from the current PDF and provably did not — hash equality is not proof that served text matches the source. The likely origin is an archived edition (every file in woollahra/v1.3-2026-09-01/ carries a 'Repealed by' stamp), i.e. the exact failure detect_repealed_stamp exists to prevent, occurring three weeks ago; whether its 4-page front-matter window missed the stamp or that run bypassed the guard is NOT established and needs its own investigation. NOT REPAIRED HERE: restoring 121802 and retiring 127014 is a production write, and the direction has to be confirmed against Amendment 36 itself — the amendment is dated 21 August 2026 and the PDF that shows B3.3 live is dated 15 September 2026, i.e. AFTER it, which is the evidence that the live text is current. The re-read that would fix it is blocked: the extractor's API returned 429 'You have no credits remaining'. ⚠⚠ THE CORRECTION ABOVE WAS ITSELF WRONG, and is withdrawn. Everything from 'CORRECTED 2026-09-27' onwards in this note described a STALE FILE. Verified properly the same day by downloading the R2 object that dcp_chapter_registry.r2_current_path actually names: source-pdfs/dcps/woollahra/v1.4-2026-09-15/chapter-b3-general-development.pdf, 2,973,719 bytes, 101 pages. It says on page 21, verbatim: 'B3.3 Floorplate (Repealed)' and 'This section was repealed by Woollahra Development Control Plan 2015 (Amendment 36) on 21 August 2026', and its contents page lists 'B3.3 FLOORPLATE (REPEALED)'. So the ORIGINAL finding stands: B3.3 is repealed and row 127014 is FAITHFUL to the current source. Row 121802, carrying the old 1.65 floorplate text, is correctly is_current=FALSE - it was superseded because the council repealed it. Nothing is hidden and nothing needs restoring. WHAT WENT WRONG: the 'correction' read woollahra/chapter-b3-general-development.pdf, a TRACKED COPY IN THIS REPOSITORY - 3,477,944 bytes, 105 pages, four pages longer, predating Amendment 36. Two files, same name, different law; the repo copy is not the source and the registry does not point at it. 542 PDFs are tracked in this repo and any of them can be stale the same way. The authority is the R2 object named by r2_current_path, and nothing else. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW: DQ-116 is RIGHT to flag it - a repealed section is served as an actionable rule and it carries no control, only the notice that the control is gone. The question for a person is whether a repeal notice should be served at all, not whether the text is accurate; it is accurate. ALSO SETTLED: scripts/verify_extraction_fidelity.py correctly did NOT flag this row. Against the real PDF every one of its distinctive words is present, so its ground_ratio is 1.0. There is no defect in that checker - the earlier claim that it 'misses this row' was computed against the stale copy too. ⚠ CONTAINED, NOT DURABLY FIXED, 2026-09-27. The 2 rows are out of the served set, but nothing stops the next extraction of any chapter putting another one in: detect_repealed_section is not yet wired into the write path, only into this probe. DQ-116 reads the live served set, so a new one surfaces the moment it is served - which is why this is containment with a watch rather than a fix. The durable change is to gate at write time. Product decision behind the repair, from the user on 2026-09-27, asked directly whether a 'this control has been removed' notice belongs in a property report: no.
